questionText:
Read the following occupational ergonomics case study and answer the questions that follow:

An occupational health audit at an export garment manufacturing factory reveals alarming health complaints among 200 sewing machine operators. Over 70% of female machine stitchers suffer from chronic Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs): lower back pain, neck stiffness, shoulder impingement, and Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in the wrists. An ergonomics expert inspects the workstations and identifies severe ergonomic design flaws:
1. Sewing chairs are rigid wooden stools without lumbar backrests, forcing operators into continuous forward-stooped static kyphotic postures.
2. Foot pedals are fixed at awkward high angles, straining ankle joints and impeding venous blood return.
3. Poor task illumination (dim, flickering tubes) creates severe visual glare and eye strain, forcing operators to crane their necks close to needles.
The factory management executes an ergonomic redesign: introducing adjustable ergonomic chairs with lumbar support, adjustable angled foot pedals, glare-free LED needle task lights, and instituting mandatory 3-minute hourly stretch breaks.

Question: What essential adjustable features must the newly installed ergonomic chairs provide to relieve lumbar and spinal fatigue?

options.text: Fixed seat height with rigid vertical backrest support and unpadded steel pan
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Pneumatic height adjustment, contoured lumbar backrest support, and padded seat pan
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Ergonomic Chair Adjustability Features.

options.text: Permanent backward 60-degree seat tilt with fixed chest support frame
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Swivel base mechanism without backrest support and rigid seat pan
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Work, Livelihood and Career (Ergonomic Chair Adjustability Features):
Pneumatic height adjustment, contoured lumbar backrest support, and padded seat pan

Detailed Analysis:
Ergonomic chairs must provide adjustable seat height (allowing proper knee angle and foot support), contoured lumbar backrest support, and a padded seat pan to reduce spinal and musculoskeletal stress. Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Work, Livelihood and Career: Ergonomic Chair Adjustability Features.
solution.detailed:

Read the following occupational ergonomics case study and answer the questions that follow:

An occupational health audit at an export garment manufacturing factory reveals alarming health complaints among 200 sewing machine operators. Over 70% of female machine stitchers suffer from chronic Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WMSDs): lower back pain, neck stiffness, shoulder impingement, and Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in the wrists. An ergonomics expert inspects the workstations and identifies severe ergonomic design flaws:
1. Sewing chairs are rigid wooden stools without lumbar backrests, forcing operators into continuous forward-stooped static kyphotic postures.
2. Foot pedals are fixed at awkward high angles, straining ankle joints and impeding venous blood return.
3. Poor task illumination (dim, flickering tubes) creates severe visual glare and eye strain, forcing operators to crane their necks close to needles.
The factory management executes an ergonomic redesign: introducing adjustable ergonomic chairs with lumbar support, adjustable angled foot pedals, glare-free LED needle task lights, and instituting mandatory 3-minute hourly stretch breaks.

Question: How did inadequate, dim task lighting at the sewing needle directly exacerbate the operators' neck and upper spine pain?

options.text: Induced continuous static abduction of shoulder joints to compensate for visual shadow interference around the foot pedal area.

options.text: Triggered rapid ocular fatigue that reduced peripheral clarity, forcing operators to rotate their lower torso continuously while stitching.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Forced operators to crane their heads forward into extreme cervical flexion to view fine stitching, overloading neck extensor muscles.

For Visual Ergonomics and Neck Posture (Work, Livelihood and Career):
Visual deficits force postural compensation: workers lean close to the work surface, generating massive biomechanical torque on cervical vertebrae. Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Arrange the procedural steps followed by an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) upon receiving a workplace harassment complaint:
(A) Receipt of written complaint from the aggrieved woman within the statutory time limit
(B) Exploring conciliation option if requested by the aggrieved woman before formal inquiry
(C) Conducting formal, confidential inquiry into the complaint adhering to principles of natural justice
(D) Submitting inquiry report with findings and recommendations to the employer within 10 days of completion

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: D, B, C, A
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A, B, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: B, A, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A, C, B, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
POSH procedure follows: complaint filing (A) -> optional conciliation (B) -> formal inquiry (C) -> report submission to management (D).
Hence, Option C is correct.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

topic: Ergonomic Risk Factors and Corrective Measures
questionText:
Match the ergonomic risk factor in List I with its corrective ergonomic solution in List II:

List I:
(A) Repetitive wrist bending
(B) Screen glare and eye strain
(C) Prolonged static standing
(D) Lumbar spine strain from sitting

List II:
(I) Ergonomic wrist rest and neutral keyboard alignment
(II) Anti-glare screen filters and indirect diffused task lighting
(III) Anti-fatigue cushioned floor mats and footrests
(IV) Adjustable chair with dedicated lumbar curvature support

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Neutral keyboard angles protect wrists, anti-glare filters protect eyes, cushioned mats relieve standing fatigue, and lumbar chairs support the lower spine.
Hence, Option A is correct.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.
